idiom_name: plain object nodes with named child properties (ESTree shape) + per-type functions
implementation_notes: Ecosystem-standard JavaScript ASTs are plain objects with a type tag and named child properties - the ESTree specification defines exactly this (BinaryExpression { left, operator, right }, Program { body }) - and each operation is a function or a switch over node.type. ES classes are equally valid and add only a prototype chain (the MDN class syntax with constructor-assigned child fields), but the object form is what parsers emit and what tooling consumes; the classic visitor is replaced by one function per node type or a per-type switch. Keep named fields while nodes are few and passes are hand-written, and derive a children array from a field-name table if generic traversal is needed later.
pitfalls: There are no compile-time node types: a misspelled property (node.leftt) evaluates to undefined and only fails deep inside a later pass.
A switch over node.type without a throwing default silently ignores node types added later; the default arm is the only exhaustiveness check available.
